body:
In my opinion, this unnecessarily complicates `EditorHelpBit`/`EditorHelpBitTooltip` (especially considering the need to preserve input data in case of locale changes, see #120549). Instead, you could use the existing `p_prologue` parameter, just like how the current value is added to the debugger.

Alternatively, you could use a `VBoxContainer` containing `EditorHelpBit` and some other control. But this is more complex, especially if there are many errors/warnings.

Looking at the `p_prologue` parameter, I see that it's added underneath the title of the currently-hovered symbol. As such, I think it makes sense that it would be more dedicated to the symbol being described in the title, and not necessarily the warning the user is hovering (which may include the hovered symbol but also other symbols nearby).

If I'm following correctly, I think the second approach you described with the `VBoxContainer` is essentially what I'm doing now. Here is the current (simplified) result of `EditorHelpBitTooltip`'s `print_tree_pretty()`:
```
 ┖╴@EditorHelpBitTooltip
    ┠╴@Panel
    ┠╴@VBoxContainer
    ┃  ┠╴@RichTextLabel (Errors and warnings)
    ┃  ┖╴@EditorHelpBit
    ┃     ┠╴@RichTextLabel (Title of hovered symbol)
    ┃     ┖╴@RichTextLabel (Description of hovered symbol)
    ┖╴@Timer
```
A single `RichTextLabel` is used for all of the errors and warnings, rather than inserting a `RichTextLabel` for each individual one. Currently, the concatenated warnings and errors are passed as different strings to `make_tooltip()` so that the text coloring can be applied in the method; I could change this to accept a single string that is displayed above `EditorHelpBit`, and then format the text with BBCode before passing it to `make_tooltip()`. That would simplify both the parameter list (one parameter for diagnostics instead of two) and method body of `make_tooltip()` (more of the diagnostic string logic is moved outside of the method).

If there is no doc tooltip, `help_bit` gets created and left without a parent and never cleaned up. 
It should just not be created in that case.
The lookup word can be gotten in `ScriptTextEditor::_on_hover_tooltip_timer_timeout`, then it can just be a local variable.

It looks like this is fine, this is forwarded from TextEdit gui_input so it is local to the TextEdit. 
I'm not sure why the menu gets it differently.

If the range is a single line then it will show even if the mouse is outside of the range column, since the start/end line checks don't account for it.
I don't think that is intentional?
The logic can be something like this:
`p_line >= p_from_line && p_line <= p_to_line && (p_line > p_from_line || p_column >= p_from_column) && (p_line < p_to_line || p_column <= p_to_column))`

(TextEdit has a `_is_line_col_in_range` that I referenced, but its private. When there is unified error support there can be a helper for this.)
Or if you want, you can make a static helper function in this file for now.
Thanks for the clarification! Since the method itself is in the parent, I wasn't sure about the space it was in, but your explanation makes sense 😅

Thank you for catching the logic bug and providing the reference to the TextEdit function!

For now I've created a static helper as per your suggestion (currently in the header file for now to keep changes consolidated, although I can move it to the cpp file if you would prefer it there). I marked it with a TODO comment suggesting that in the future we try to unify it with the TextEdit version since they are effectively the same, but don't want to go changing too much outside of what this PR specifically aims to do (i.e., changing a bunch of function calls in TextEdit unrelated to the tooltip functionality). That being said, if you'd prefer I just take care of that migration now for this PR, I can do that instead!
The error and warning messages should be bbcode escaped. ```suggestion diagnostic_strings_concatenated += String("\n").join(error_strings).replace("[", "[lb]"); ```
This can check `Input::get_singleton()->is_anything_pressed()` like CodeEdit does.
